blocks.text: During a chemical reaction reactants are converted into products, so the concentration of the products rises as that of the reactants falls.

blocks.title: Rate of reaction
blocks.text: The rate of a reaction is the change in the concentration of a reactant or a product divided by the time taken for the change: rate = delta x / delta t, where delta x is a very small change in concentration in a very small time interval delta t.

For a reactant A changing irreversibly to a product B, the slope of the concentration-time graph is steepest at the beginning, showing a rapid fall in the reactant and a rapid rise in the product; as the reaction proceeds the slope becomes less steep, the reaction slows with time, and finally both curves become parallel at the completion of the reaction. So the rate of a reaction changes every moment. The units of rate are concentration divided by time, usually mol dm-3 s-1; for slow reactions mol dm-3 min-1 or mol dm-3 h-1 may be used, and for gas-phase reactions units of pressure replace molar concentration. For A giving B the rate can be written as the rate of disappearance of A or the rate of appearance of B: rate = -delta[A]/delta t = +delta[B]/delta t, the negative sign showing the decrease in the reactant's concentration and the positive sign the increase in the product's.

blocks.alt: Left: a red curve of reactant concentration falling and a blue curve of product rising against time, steep at first and flattening to parallel. Right: the seven HI concentrations of Table 7.1 plotted against time with a dashed tangent at 100 seconds and a green right-angled triangle giving 0.04 mol dm-3 over 100 s.
blocks.caption: Concentration against time for a reactant and a product, and the tangent method on the HI decomposition data (original diagram after Figures 7.1 and 7.2 and Table 7.1).
blocks.long_description: The reactant curve falls and the product curve rises, both fastest at the start; their slopes shrink as the reactants are used up until the curves run level at completion. The rate at any instant is the slope of the curve there, found by drawing a tangent and completing a triangle: at 100 seconds the tangent falls by 0.04 mol dm-3 over about 160 seconds, a rate of about 2.5 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1 (the print works this out as 4 x 10^-4). The product curve gives the same value at the same time.

blocks.prompt: Hydrogen and iodine form hydrogen iodide, H2 + I2 giving 2HI. In the first 100.0 s the iodine concentration falls from 0.010 to 0.0080 mol dm-3. What is the average rate over this period?

items: Rate = change in concentration / time, in mol dm-3 s-1 (per min or per h for slow reactions, pressure units for gases); rate = -delta[A]/delta t = +delta[B]/delta t.
Concentration-time curves are steepest at the start and flatten to parallel at completion, so the rate falls continuously.
